source.title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
source.authors: Alan Chen; Jack Merullo; Alessandro Stolfo; Ellie Pavlick

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representational transfer with affine stitching and downstream evaluations, rather than measuring convergence with the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: Rows cover stitch fidelity, transferred SAE reconstruction, probe and steering transfer, and feature-level transfer results. Cited results from other papers and the stitch-layer selection SVCCA values are not recorded as findings. Values for probes and several feature analyses are reported only in figures, so those rows retain figure-only values.
record.test_reason: The study learns affine stitches between residual streams of within-family LMs of different sizes (Pythia, GPT2, Gemma-2). It measures downstream loss, transferred-SAE quality, probe and steering transfer, and whether specific features keep their function. These results bear directly on V4 (a simple linear map with little loss) and on V5 (features recurring across models). Variation by language, dataset and token distribution bears on the input-dependence part of V6. It does not measure a trend with scale, so V1 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that affine stitches faithfully map between same-family LMs of different sizes, supporting 'weak universality', and can transfer SAEs, probes and steering vectors. Transferred SAEs are imperfect but cut SAE training FLOPs by about 50% when used as initialization. Performance is bottlenecked by the smaller model. Semantic and structural features transfer differently, while specific functional features keep their roles. Probe and steering transfer works only in specific cases, and cross-family transfer is left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses concurrent affine residual-stream mappings trained with reconstruction and inversion losses, then tests downstream fidelity and feature transfer. The tested models are within-family pairs trained on the same data; this is not the original studies' similarity-measure procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies with model pair and direction, feature class (semantic versus structural), language pair and frequency, and task (response-language versus instruction-following steering).

fits_no_version.finding: Initializing an SAE on the larger model from a stitched small-model SAE reaches high explained-variance thresholds with about 30-50% fewer FLOPs. Stitch-initialized features rotate less during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representations shared across model sizes can be exploited to cut interpretability training cost (tool use, not a convergence rate).

record.problems: Evidence is restricted to selected within-family, same-data model pairs; cross-family transfer is explicitly left for future work. Some probe, feature, and instruction-following outcomes are shown only in plots. The language-steering evaluation uses a subset of 163 prompts, and the authors note wide confidence intervals for the small IFEval set. Feature analysis is described as correlational and its semantic/structural classification as imperfect.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted to meet the 60-row cap. Other values in Tables 5 and 6 are not individually extracted; representative language-pair rows are retained to show the explicitly reported variation across conditions.

untested.parts: Whole version: there is no trend of alignment across model scale or capability. Only one same-data pair per family is tested.
Whole version: there are no vision or paired image-caption data.
Whole version: there are no different-seed comparisons.
Cross-family or cross-data mapping, relative representations, mapping without paired data.
Broad recurrence of features across many independently trained models. Only a few GPT2 features are analysed in depth.
Dependence on the similarity measure or its settings (e.g. neighbours). SVCCA is used only for layer selection, and the layer choice is not varied.
Whole version: plateau is not tested, and the causal role of shared data or objectives is not isolated, since all pairs share data. The incompleteness of transfer is recorded under V4.

missing.what: Attribution-correlation histograms show most transferred features far above a random-SAE baseline, with some features flipped or untransferred, for all three pairs.
Positive correlation between a language's frequency in training data and its relative steering transfer gap, in both directions.
Remaining language pairs in Tables 5-6, e.g. 9b→2b el 0.48 vs GT 0.85, hu 0.06 vs 0.72. Also the averaged steering result in Fig 3b and the bimodal transfer-gap distribution in Fig 3c.
A dense probe trained on pythia-70m and applied zero-shot to down-stitched 160m activations nearly matches a probe trained on 160m.

record.verdict_notes: All pairs are same-family, same-data, same-tokenizer, so the study cannot speak to convergence across independent training (V1) or to its causes (V7). For rows linked to both V4 and V6 (r19-r30), the recorded state describes transfer success for V4. The V6 verdict rests on the contrast between rows, not on each row's state. In r28 the 9b ground-truth en-fr steering is 0.09 while the transfer reaches 0.69, an anomaly in the source table. The stitch layer is chosen by maximum SVCCA, a selection step and not a finding.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test alignment increasing across a broad scale range or its relation to independently measured capability; models are within the same family and trained on the same data.
No paired image-caption or vision-language model representations.
No comparison of different random seeds of the same architecture.
Tests affine stitching and transfer of SAEs, probes, and steering vectors between selected language models; does not test relative representations or transfer without paired data.
Analyzes selected SAE features and functional roles; does not establish recurrence of a broad set of neurons, SAE features, or circuits across many independently trained models.
Shows variation by feature category and language/task, but does not compare multiple similarity measures or systematically test neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
Tests selected same-family, same-data model pairs; does not isolate the causal contribution of shared training data or objectives from other factors.

relationships.condition: Round-trip stitches, GPT2 direct round trips, high-frequency language steering, and sparse probes (within-family, same-data pairs)
relationships.reason: Round trips are near-lossless (r3, r7, r8, r11). Transferred steering nearly matches ground truth for de and fr (r22, r24, r26, r28). Transferred probes beat random on most datasets (r19, r20).
relationships.display_finding: Round trips were nearly lossless, German and French steering transferred effectively, and sparse probes outperformed random transfer on most datasets.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Round-trip stitches, GPT2 direct round trips, high-frequency language steering, and sparse probes (within-family, same-data pairs)
source_check.reason: The condition group mixes successful and partial transfer. Retain supports for r3,r7,r8,r11,r22,r24,r26,r28, and separate the partial sparse-probe results r19,r20 as limits_scope. Beating random does not establish little loss. Also, r28 exceeds native steering (0.69 versus 0.09), rather than nearly matching it.

relationships.condition: Direct A→B / B→A stitches and B→A→B round trips, zero-shot SAE transfer, low-frequency languages, IFEval instruction steering
relationships.reason: Direct stitches cost +8% to +39% CE (r1, r2, r5, r6, r9, r10), and reverse round trips +4.7% and +13% (r4, r12). Transferred SAE FUV roughly doubles to triples (r13-r18). Steering transfer is near zero for bg and et (r21, r23, r25, r27), and instruction-steering transfer is weak (r29, r30).
relationships.display_finding: Direct stitches increased cross-entropy by 8–39% and reverse round trips by 4.7% and 13%; transferred SAE unexplained variance roughly doubled to tripled, steering transfer was near zero for bg and et, and instruction steering transferred weakly.

source_check.reason: §5.1 and Figures 4,14,15 show feature-dependent correspondence: structural features transfer more consistently, while some semantic features fail to transfer or have flipped attribution correlations (r31).

relationships.condition: Input dependence: languages, probing datasets, and chat-template tokens outside the stitch's training data
relationships.reason: Transfer succeeds for de and fr but vanishes for bg and et (r21-r28). Probes fail on code and language datasets (r19, r20). IFEval transfer is weak, which the authors attribute to out-of-distribution template tokens (r29, r30). The frequency correlation in Fig 11 comes from the text.
relationships.display_finding: Transfer succeeded for German and French but vanished for Bulgarian and Estonian, while probes failed on code and language datasets; IFEval transfer was weak, which the authors attributed to out-of-distribution template tokens.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Input dependence: languages, probing datasets, and chat-template tokens outside the stitch's training data
source_check.reason: Probing varies by domain (r19,r20); language steering succeeds for de/fr and fails for bg/et (r21–r28); instruction-steering transfer is weak (r29,r30). Figure 11 reports a positive frequency correlation. Appendix F.2 presents unseen chat-template tokens as a conjectured explanation, with small datasets and noisy vectors as additional limitations.

relation.reason: The study directly evaluates mapping fidelity, functional-feature preservation, and variation in transfer across input domains and tasks.

tranche.reason: Concurrent affine stitches with reconstruction and inversion objectives, evaluated through downstream fidelity and feature transfer, test representational interchangeability using a different method.

source_check.notes: Tests concern within-family models trained on the same data; cross-family generalization is untested. Appendix H contains an experimental generation prompt, not instructions to the checker.

statements.correction: Table 1: A→B→A increases CE by <1% for all three pairs. B→A→B increases CE by 1.4% for GPT2, 4.7% for Pythia, and 13% for Gemma.
statements.problem: The round-trip claim omits direction-dependent exceptions: not all tested within-family round trips are near-lossless.

statements.correction: Table 1: direct-stitch CE increases range from 8.3% to 39%; partial transfer supports limits_scope. Tables 5–6: bg and et transferred steering is approximately at the no-steering baseline, warranting challenges for those conditions. Appendix F.2: instruction steering is weak overall, with some improvements over no steering.
statements.problem: The factual summary is correct, but the challenges label combines absent steering effects with partial transfer results that warrant limits_scope.
